newsitem.title: LEBANON: EU envoy says his formula can revive peace talks.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy says his formula can revive peace talks.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos said on Monday his "full withdrawal for full security" formula could revive stalled Israeli-Syrian peace talks.

Moratinos told reporters during a stopover in Beirut that his idea was well received by Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez. He was in the Lebanese capital after talks with Israeli and Syrian leaders.
"I think that it evidently is a formula that can satisfy all parties, the Syrian, the Lebanese and the Israeli authorities because everybody will get what they are searching for," Moratinos said.
"Some seek the withdrawal of occupation from their territories, and others seek total security," he said.
Moratinos said Israel was considering the proposal, although Israel's Likud government has previously ruled out full return of the occupied Golan Heights to Syria.
Moratinos arrived from Damascus where he held talks with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara. An official accompanying him said the talks were "very positive".
"If the idea is full withdrawal in exchange for full security...without imposed Israeli security conditions in the (freed) areas, then it might be a good idea," Bouez said.

Moratinos said the formula called for total withdrawal from the occupied Arab lands in return for total, equal and mutual security for all parties and was "an attempt to create some dynamism in the region."

Syria has said the previous Israeli government agreed to return the Golan Heights captured in 1967 and talks should resume where Israel broke them off in February 1996. Israel says it wants talks with no preconditions.
Lebanese-Israeli peace talks are similarly deadlocked over an Israeli pullout from a 15-km (nine mile)-wide occupation zone in south Lebanon.
